Hi! I'm Amin , I've always been fascinated by space. For this challenge I built Mission Designer 3D, a game where you design a spacecraft, launch it, and try to beat what NASA achieved on real missions. I'm looking for people who: knows (science and engineering backgrounds are very welcome)
enjoy design, 3D, storytelling and can help explain the science. Message me , to participate
summary:
Mission Designer is a browser game where players become the chief engineer of a real space mission. They design a robotic spacecraft by choosing the rocket, engine, fuel, power system and science instruments, then launch it and fly the mission week by week, fixing faults along the way. Five missions are included, from the Moon to Mars, plus a guided Training Flight for first-time players.

The game addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by making trade-offs visible. Mass, power, cost, data and fuel are linked, so one change affects the whole mission. Results come from real physics: the rocket equation, Hohmann transfers, gravity, air load at Max-Q and solar power. It uses NASA data such as Moon and Mars gravity, size and distance, and the masses of the LRO and MRO spacecraft. Players compare their score with the real NASA mission.

It matters because mission design is hard for students to picture. Mission Designer lets anyone learn by playing, on a phone or a computer, with no install.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
Mission Designer lets the player act as the chief engineer of a space mission. In 3 steps the player builds a spacecraft (vehicle and storage, science and comms, then power and safety), launches it, and flies the mission week by week. Faults happen along the way, such as a solar array failure, and the player must choose how to repair them using the spare materials they packed. At the end the score is compared with the real NASA mission.

HOW IT WORKS
The player chooses a launch vehicle (4 to pick from), an engine (hydrazine, bipropellant or xenon ion), single or two-stage, fuel, solar panels, dish, battery, recorder and up to 7 science instruments. The game then calculates the result from physics: the rocket equation, Hohmann transfer orbits, planet gravity, air load at Max-Q, solar power at each distance, and the data that fits through the radio downlink. A Ship Check panel warns about problems before launch, and a Chain Map shows how mass, power, data and cost are linked.

MISSIONS
5 missions plus a guided Training Flight, from the Moon to Mars, each with its own budget and science goal.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Students learn real mission design by playing instead of reading long text. It runs in a web browser on phones and computers, with no install.

TOOLS
HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with our own 3D spacecraft view. Presentation built with three.js. AI (Claude) helped with code and text.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE
Every choice has a cost somewhere else, and the game lets players see that and fix their mistakes.
